title: Export the committed supervisor effect surface from @moe/runner root
description:
Objective: publish child 1's committed supervisor effect surface on the @moe/runner package root so apps/daemon can compose it. Blocker-fix task 2 of 3 for task-ba3a45f9 (Daemon work services, SPIDR child 3). Created by architect-8a4a1764 2026-08-08 under human approval in the REPL. Siblings: task-8ee125d0 (scheduler surface, independent, also ready now) and the .js bridge sweep task (gated on child 2).

WHY THIS EXISTS. packages/runner/src/index.ts exports only the artifacts, scope, and workspace surfaces. The supervisor/ subtree is deliberately NOT exported - child 1's decision, QA-confirmed in mem:task-task-2580a578812f46a49cae0af79ff6fc16-qa-verdict ("Nothing added to packages/runner/src/index.ts - supervisor stays internal, claude modules are precedent"). packages/runner/package.json pins "exports": {".": "./src/index.ts"}, an EXCLUSIVE map: no deep subpath import reaches around it, at runtime or under moduleResolution NodeNext. Probed on the identically-shaped sibling package from apps/daemon: import('@moe/scheduler/authority/lease-resource.js') -> ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED, while import('@moe/scheduler') -> OK. Internal-by-default was correct while nothing consumed the subtree; task-ba3a45f9 is the first consumer, so the seam gets published deliberately.

THIS TASK IS READY NOW - it does NOT wait on SPIDR child 2. Two verified reasons:
  1. task-ba3a45f9's DoD needs only CHILD 1's records - effect intent creation, the lifecycle command surface, and the one-use activation gate. Child 2's launch-lock / drain / restart modules appear nowhere in child 3's Definition of Done. Child 1 is COMMITTED at 72545bb and stable.
  2. Child 2's approved plan declares 9 files, ALL under packages/runner/src/supervisor/ (launch-lock.ts, drain-reconciliation.ts, drain-table.ts, restart-reconstruction.ts + tests, plus edits to effect-kernel.ts and effect-lifecycle.ts). packages/runner/src/index.ts is NOT among them. Zero file collision.
Child 2 does append new codes to the frozen vocabularies inside effect-kernel.ts. That is safe for this task: appending members to an already-exported array does not change the set of export NAMES, so the surface test specified below stays green.

Deliverable: a curated named-export block in packages/runner/src/index.ts, in the style the file already uses (named exports grouped per module, types in the same block via the `type` modifier, every specifier written with the .js extension per NodeNext). Export from the seven committed child-1 modules - effect-kernel.js, effect-shape.js, effect-parse.js, effect-lifecycle.js, effect-grant.js, effect-activation.js, lease-mirror.js - the records, pure functions, and error-code vocabularies a caller needs to: create an effect intent, apply a lifecycle command and discriminate all three LifecycleOutcome kinds (TRANSITIONED | MUST_DRAIN | REFUSED), consume and validate a one-use activation grant, and mirror-fence a lease. Read the modules and mem:task-task-2580a578812f46a49cae0af79ff6fc16-handoff for the exact surface; do not guess names. Prefer curated named exports over a blanket `export *` so the published seam stays a reviewed decision. Do NOT export effect-test-fixtures.ts - test-only.

NOT in scope: any .js bridge (that is the separate sweep task - do not add one here, it would be a partial sweep whose incompleteness is invisible to the test gate); changing ANY behaviour in any supervisor module; exporting child 2's in-flight modules; touching packages/scheduler; touching apps/daemon; any package.json or lockfile edit.

Hard dependencies: none. Child 1 (task-2580a578) is COMMITTED at 72545bb.

Owned paths: packages/runner/src/index.ts, packages/runner/src/index-surface.test.ts (new).
Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/runner test && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck
definitionOfDone: packages/runner/src/index.ts exports the child-1 supervisor surface such that a consumer can, without any deep subpath import, create an effect intent, apply a lifecycle command and discriminate all three LifecycleOutcome kinds by name, consume and validate a one-use activation grant, and call the lease mirror - naming every parameter type and every union branch of every exported function's return type.

A new packages/runner/src/index-surface.test.ts imports the package ROOT specifier @moe/runner (never a relative or deep path) and asserts per symbol that the export is present and of the expected typeof, so a dropped export fails by name rather than by a vague count.

The same test asserts set equality between Object.keys of the namespace and a hand-written expected export-name list, so both a removed export AND an unreviewed addition go red. The list is hand-transcribed from the modules, never derived from the namespace under test (mem:gotcha-self-derived-universe-cannot-check-itself).

The three LifecycleOutcome kinds remain structurally discriminable through the published surface: a test asserts a REFUSED outcome has exactly the keys [kind, failure] and that MUST_DRAIN carries no ok field - the properties child 1 relied on so that ok === false cannot mistake a drain instruction for a refusal. Asserted against the exported production surface, not a local re-declaration.

Zero behaviour change: git diff shows packages/runner/src/index.ts as the only modified non-test file, no .js file is added, effect-test-fixtures.ts is not exported, and the pre-existing runner suite passes with a test count greater than or equal to the pre-task count, stated as an explicit before/after number.

pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/runner test && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck exits 0; committed paths are exactly packages/runner/src/index.ts and packages/runner/src/index-surface.test.ts.
taskRails: Re-export only. This task changes what is REACHABLE, never what any function DOES. No .ts file other than index.ts may be edited. If a symbol seems to need a signature change to be exportable, report_blocked rather than editing a supervisor module - child 2 is working in that directory right now.

Do NOT add any .js bridge. @moe/runner is unloadable by plain Node today and the fix is a package-wide sweep owned by a separate task gated on child 2; a partial sweep here would be silently incomplete and invisible to the test gate (mem:gotcha-runner-package-does-not-load-under-plain-node). This task's gate is vitest, which does not need bridges.

Read packages/runner/src/supervisor/*.ts and mem:task-task-2580a578812f46a49cae0af79ff6fc16-handoff before naming a single symbol. Do not guess export names - verify each one exists (skill: explore-before-assume).
Never export a test-only module. effect-test-fixtures.ts stays internal; exporting it puts test code on the runtime surface.

Assert against the production surface, not a reimplementation: the LifecycleOutcome shape assertions must run on values obtained through the @moe/runner root import, never on a locally re-declared type or fixture copy (epic rail 6).

Keep the production file focused: target <=250 lines, split before 400. If the added exports push packages/runner/src/index.ts past 250 lines, extract a supervisor re-export module that index.ts re-exports rather than letting the entry point sprawl.

Commit by explicit pathspec only - git commit -- packages/runner/src/index.ts packages/runner/src/index-surface.test.ts. Never a bare git commit; child 2 has uncommitted work in this package and the index is shared state (epic rail 3). Verify with git show --stat afterwards.

implementationPlan.description: Re-verify the surface on disk before naming a symbol — child 2 is committing into this directory, so this note may already be stale. Read all seven child-1 modules (effect-kernel, effect-shape, effect-parse, effect-lifecycle, effect-grant, effect-activation, lease-mirror) and record every exported value and type. TWO THINGS TO CHECK SPECIFICALLY. First, `effect-activation.ts:36` contains its own `export { ... }` re-export block: read it, because a name re-exported from both effect-activation.js and its original module would be a duplicate export and a compile error that reads like a mystery. Second, confirm that child 2's edits only APPENDED members to the frozen vocabularies rather than renaming or removing any export — appended members are safe for this task (the set of export NAMES is unchanged), a rename or removal is not, and per rail 1 the response to that is report_blocked, never editing a supervisor module. Then make the one judgement call this task contains: decide whether effect-shape's generic validators (isStrictRecord, exactRecord, isRef, isDigest, isCount, oneOf, readList, readOwnDataProperty, hasOnlyOwnStringKeys, isPlainArray) belong on a public seam. DoD 1 names only intent creation, lifecycle commands, grant consumption and lease fencing; publishing internal helpers widens the package API permanently for no stated consumer. Record the decision and its reason in the step note. Produce no code.

Hand-transcribe the expected export-name list — a separate step, deliberately, because DoD 3 lives or dies on this. Write the complete list of names index.ts will publish, taken BY HAND from the module sources you just read, and record it in the step note. Do NOT generate it from `Object.keys()` of anything, do not paste it from a namespace dump, and do not derive it from the export block you are about to write: a list derived from the thing under test asserts only that the namespace equals itself and can never fail (mem:gotcha-self-derived-universe-cannot-check-itself). This list is simultaneously the specification for step 4's export block and the expected value for step 3's set-equality assertion, and it must be written before either. Cross-check it against the decision recorded in step 1 about the effect-shape validators so the list and the export block cannot disagree.

TDD red — create packages/runner/src/index-surface.test.ts. FIRST, prove the mechanism before building on it: write one trivial assertion that `import * as runner from "@moe/runner"` resolves at all. That self-referencing ROOT specifier is required by DoD 2 and is the single point of failure for this whole task; if it does not resolve under this vitest config, STOP and report it rather than falling back to a relative or deep import — a relative import would make the suite green while testing nothing about the published seam, which is the entire deliverable. Once it resolves, assert per symbol from the step-2 list that the export is present and of the expected `typeof`, so a dropped export fails BY NAME rather than by a vague count. Then DoD 3's two-way guard: assert set equality between `Object.keys` of the namespace and the hand-written list, so a removed export AND an unreviewed addition both go red. Red, because index.ts does not export the supervisor surface yet.

Add the curated supervisor export block to packages/runner/src/index.ts, matching the file's existing style exactly: one grouped `export { ... } from "./supervisor/<module>.js";` block per module, value exports first and `type` entries in the same braces, every specifier carrying the `.js` extension per NodeNext. Export from the seven committed child-1 modules exactly the names on the step-2 list — the records, pure functions and error-code vocabularies a caller needs to create an effect intent, apply a lifecycle command and discriminate all three LifecycleOutcome kinds, consume and validate a one-use activation grant, and mirror-fence a lease. Prefer curated named exports over a blanket `export *`, so the published seam stays a reviewed decision rather than whatever the modules happen to export next week. Do NOT export effect-test-fixtures.ts — test-only code must never reach the runtime surface. Do NOT add any .js bridge file (rail 2): @moe/runner genuinely is unloadable under plain Node today, but that is a package-wide defect owned by task-eb9ff081, and a partial sweep here would be silently incomplete and invisible to this task's vitest gate. index.ts is 70 lines today and should land near 150; if it bursts 250, extract a supervisor re-export module per rail 6 rather than letting the entry point sprawl.

Prove the LifecycleOutcome union survives publication — DoD 4, the one behavioural property this task must not silently break. Through values obtained from the `@moe/runner` ROOT import (never a local re-declaration and never a fixture copy — epic rail 6 requires the assertion to run on the production surface), assert that all three kinds remain structurally discriminable by name: TRANSITIONED, MUST_DRAIN and REFUSED. Assert specifically that a REFUSED outcome has exactly the keys [kind, failure], and that MUST_DRAIN carries NO `ok` field. Those are the exact properties child 1 relied on so that a consumer testing `ok === false` cannot mistake a drain instruction for a refusal — MUST_DRAIN is an instruction to drain, not a rejected command, and collapsing the two would be a real correctness regression introduced purely by how the seam was published. Obtain the outcomes by calling the exported applyEffectCommand with inputs that produce each kind, rather than by constructing outcome literals, so the test exercises the real union.

Prove zero behaviour change — DoD 5, stated as numbers rather than as a claim. Record the runner suite's test count BEFORE this task's changes (from the pre-task run) and AFTER, and state both explicitly in the completion evidence; the after count must be greater than or equal to the before count, since this task only adds a suite. Then confirm with `git status --porcelain` and `git diff --stat` that packages/runner/src/index.ts is the ONLY modified non-test file, that NO .js file was added anywhere, and that effect-test-fixtures.ts appears in no export. Confirm no .ts file under supervisor/ was touched — rail 1 forbids it and child 2 is working in that directory right now, so any diff there is either a mistake or a collision. Also confirm with wc -l (not PowerShell Measure-Object -Line, which skips blank lines and only ever reports room) that index.ts stayed under the 250 target, or that the rail-6 extraction was performed if it did not.

Run the full gate for this task, which deliberately includes the daemon typecheck: pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/runner test && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck. Run it fresh from the repo root and capture the real output as evidence. The daemon typecheck is in the gate for a reason — this task exists so apps/daemon can compose the supervisor surface, and a surface that publishes but does not typecheck from its intended consumer has not done its job. Attribute red by path and never by a remembered count: `packages/runner/src/supervisor/` is shared with child 2 right now, so red there is likely theirs — check before claiming or fixing it, and never edit a foreign test or module to make your suite green. The scope-observation real-git test has a known 5s-timeout flake on this machine: re-run once, report the result, do not chase it. Anything red in index.ts or index-surface.test.ts is unambiguously yours.

Adversarial self-review, then commit by explicit pathspec. Read the diff as an attacker: is the expected export-name list genuinely hand-written, or did it get derived from the namespace it checks; does the test import the ROOT specifier `@moe/runner` everywhere, with no relative or deep path anywhere in the file; is any test-only module exported; is any name exported twice from two modules; did any supervisor .ts file get edited; was a .js bridge added anywhere; can a consumer still discriminate all three LifecycleOutcome kinds and still distinguish MUST_DRAIN from REFUSED; does the published set match the hand-written list in BOTH directions so an unreviewed addition also goes red. Then stage and commit by EXPLICIT PATHSPEC — `git commit -- packages/runner/src/index.ts packages/runner/src/index-surface.test.ts` — never a bare git commit, never git commit -a, never git add -A, and never a directory pathspec under packages/runner/src/, because child 2 has uncommitted work throughout this package and the index is shared state. Run `git status --porcelain` first and unstage any foreign path with `git restore --staged`. Verify with `git show --stat` that exactly those two paths landed and no probe, scratch or debug file is present.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
(1) CURATED NAMED EXPORTS, NOT `export *` — the task specifies this and the existing file already demonstrates the style: named exports grouped per module, types inline via the `type` modifier, every specifier written with a `.js` extension per NodeNext. A blanket re-export would publish whatever a module happens to export today and silently republish whatever it exports tomorrow, which is exactly what DoD 3's set-equality assertion exists to prevent.
(2) SELF-REFERENCING IMPORT IS THE POINT, AND IS THE ONE THING THAT MIGHT NOT WORK — DoD 2 requires the test to import the package ROOT specifier `@moe/runner`, never a relative path, because the whole defect being fixed is that `exports: {".": "./src/index.ts"}` is an EXCLUSIVE map and deep subpath imports are unreachable. Node supports self-reference by package name when the package declares `exports`, and vitest resolves workspace packages, so this should work — but verify it in step 3 before building the whole suite on it. If self-reference does not resolve under this vitest config, that is a real finding: report it rather than quietly downgrading to a relative import, because a relative import would make the test pass while testing nothing about the published seam.
(3) SIZE — index.ts is 70 lines today; the child-1 surface is roughly 60-70 specifiers, landing around 140-150 lines. That is inside the 250 target, so no extraction is needed. Rail 6's escape hatch (a supervisor re-export module) applies only if it actually bursts 250.
(4) NO BRIDGES HERE, deliberately — and the reason is not 'they are unnecessary'. @moe/runner genuinely IS unloadable under plain Node today; that is a real defect owned by task-eb9ff081 as a package-wide sweep. A partial sweep in this task would be silently incomplete and invisible to the vitest gate, which is strictly worse than none.

If it does not resolve under this vitest config, report it — do NOT silently fall back to a relative or deep import, because that would make the suite pass while testing nothing about the published seam, which is the whole deliverable.
2. **Duplicate exports are a compile error, and effect-activation.ts already re-exports.** Read its `export {}` block at line 36 before composing index.ts; a name re-exported from both effect-kernel.js and effect-activation.js will fail typecheck in a way that reads like a mystery.

If you generate it from `Object.keys(namespace)`, the test asserts that the namespace equals itself and can never fail. Write it by hand, in a separate step, before the test that consumes it.
4. **Child 2 is actively committing in `packages/runner/src/supervisor/`.** Re-read the seven modules at step 1 rather than trusting this note. Appended array members are safe; a RENAMED or REMOVED export would break you, and the fix is to report it, never to edit a supervisor module (rail 1).

Publishing them widens the package's public API permanently for no stated consumer need; DoD 1 names only what a caller needs to create an intent, apply a command, consume a grant and fence a lease. Prefer excluding them and say so in the evidence — but whatever you choose, the hand-written list and the export block must agree.
6. **Never export effect-test-fixtures.ts** (rail 4) — test-only code on the runtime surface.
7. **Do not add a .js bridge** (rail 2). @moe/runner really is unloadable under plain Node today, but that is a package-wide defect owned by task-eb9ff081; a partial sweep here would be invisible to this task's vitest gate and worse than nothing.
